headlines.text: It was 2023 when the inaugural AEW Continental Title was crowned as Eddie Kingston vs. Jon Moxley went to war, appearing on Worlds End, rated 8.14 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. In the tournament final of the inaugural Continental Classic, Kingston defeated Moxley to become the first-ever American Triple Crown Champion, unifying the AEW Continental, ROH World, and NJPW Strong Openweight Titles.

On a Wednesday in 2020, back when Proud-N-Powerful & MJF made their AEW debut as a team, appearing on Dynamite, rated 9.17 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype. Part of AEW's deeply emotional "Celebration of Life" episode for Brodie Lee, with Brodie Jr. wearing a Dark Order mask and cheering ringside ? MJF played the perfect heel foil throughout the night's tribute matches, a poignant moment even amid the storyline mischief.

On a Friday in 2022, back when Orange Cassidy vs. Trent Beretta clashed for the AEW All-Atlantic Title, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.30 ? a well-worked match. Orange Cassidy was chasing gold for the 10th time. Best Friends collided as Cassidy defended the All-Atlantic Title against his own stablemate Trent, who stormed off unable to hide his frustration after the loss.

secondaries.text: On this day in 2023, a new champion was crowned for the AEW TNT Title as Adam Copeland vs. Christian Cage battled it out in a No DQ match, appearing on Worlds End, rated 8.37 ? one of the better matches of the year ? ending the champion's reign at 5 defenses. In a No DQ match filled with tables, ladders and Shayna Wayne interference, Copeland speared Cage through a table to win his first title in over a decade ? only to lose it right back moments later when Killswitch's contract loophole let Cage steal it with a Spear of his own.

Rewind to 2023, when a new champion was crowned for the AEW World Heavyweight Title as Samoa Joe vs. MJF battled it out, appearing on Worlds End, rated 7.05 ? a well-worked match ? ending the champion's reign at 11 defenses. Samoa Joe choked out a battered MJF to end his 400-plus-day reign and win the AEW World Championship, as Adam Cole's unmasking as The Devil loomed over the entire match.

Looking back to 2023, when Claudio Castagnoli reached a real marker of consistency: their 50th match in AEW, facing Castagnoli & Danielson vs. Bryan Danielson vs. Claudio Castagnoli vs. Daniel Garcia vs. Mark Briscoe vs. Brody King vs. Jay Lethal vs. Jay White vs. Rush, setting the tone as the night's opener on Worlds End, rated 7.32 ? a well-worked match ? part of that year's Worlds End '23.
